newsitem.title: UK: Britain's Horlick gets Ely Fund Managers job - paper.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Horlick gets Ely Fund Managers job - paper.

text.p: Nicola Horlick, the former managing director of Morgan Grenfell Asset Management (MGAM) who was suspended in January after being accused by her ex-employer of planning a mass defection to ABN Amro, has a new job at Ely Fund Managers, said The Guardian on Friday.

The woman dubbed "Superwoman" by the British media because of her past ability to hold down one of the biggest jobs in the City of London and raise five children, has joined the small fund management house called Ely, said the report.
Ely manages around 250 million pounds of private investor funds compared to the 18 billion she controlled when at MGAM, which is a subsidiary of Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
The report coincides with another in The Times on Friday which said a senior ABN Amro director had finally admitted that he made a job offer to Horlick.
The Times said Rijnhard van Tets, a member of the managing board of ABN Amro, said he had approached Horlick about a job but did not try and poach her entire team at MGAM.
Horlick was suspended by MGAM's parent group DMG on January 14 just days after being promoted managing director of MGAM amid allegations that she planned to defect and take her team with her.

The report quoted van Tets saying "I had a meeting with Ms Horlick about her herself and not her team. I am not a believer in poaching teams and I have never done that. Nor would I try to disrupt their business."

Horlick was quoted in the report responding "I did meet van Tets unexpectedly at the Lanesborough Hotel in London on the evening of Wednesday January 8. He basically said he would like me to run the global asset management business of ABN Amro."
She has denied allegations that she tried to poach staff. DMG has said in the past it has no plans to compensate or reinstate her.
